slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Two paper cutouts of the same scalene triangle, one flipped and turned. Students tape them together edge to edge and write which corner landed on which, then compare their letter lists with a partner.

  • Given a congruence statement such as triangle ABC ≅ triangle EFD, I can list all six pairs of corresponding parts by reading letter positions.
  • I can explain why triangle ABC ≅ triangle FED and triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF say different things, and use = only for lengths and angle measures.

geo.body:
Two paper cutouts of the same scalene triangle, one flipped and turned. Students tape them together edge to edge and write which corner landed on which, then compare their letter lists with a partner.

  • Given a congruence statement such as triangle ABC ≅ triangle EFD, I can list all six pairs of corresponding parts by reading letter positions.
  • I can explain why triangle ABC ≅ triangle FED and triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF say different things, and use = only for lengths and angle measures.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: a congruence statement is an ordered matching. Position 1 matches position 1, and so on. Show ≅ for figures and = for lengths and measures, side by side.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Use a match to find x (original problem).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle PQR, with AB = 2x + 1 and PQ = 9.Given.
AB matches PQ, so 2x + 1 = 9.1st and 2nd letters match 1st and 2nd letters.
2x = 8, so x = 4.Subtract 1, then divide by 2.
BC = 7 matches QR, so QR = 7. PR = 10 matches AC, so AC = 10.Same position rule.
Nothing says BC equals PR.BC and PR are not in matching positions.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan writes triangle ABC ≅ triangle FED for the cutouts. Find the mismatch.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

Jordan wrote triangle ABC ≅ triangle FED. That is not just a new order. It says A matches F, which is false here. Write triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF only when those letters really match. Use = for lengths and angle measures, and ≅ for figures.

slides.title: Practice 1
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle XYZ and BC = 12. Find YZ.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

B goes with Y and C goes with Z, so YZ = BC = 12.

Reveal second check

Read it backward: YZ matches BC.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Triangle PQR ≅ triangle LMN and angle Q = 37 degrees. Find angle M.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Q is in the middle, and so is M. So angle M = 37 degrees.

Reveal second check

The middle letters match in both lists.

slides.title: Practice 3
slides.html:
Triangle ABC ≅ triangle DEF, AC = 3x - 2 and DF = 13. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

AC matches DF, so 3x - 2 = 13. Then 3x = 15 and x = 5.

Reveal second check

Plug in: 3(5) - 2 = 13.

geo.solution: AC matches DF, so 3x - 2 = 13. Then 3x = 15 and x = 5.
